lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: They're broadcasting. All of them at once.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Multiple signals. Same vector signature. Same... Jesus.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: The signal's fragmenting. I'm reading at least fifty distinct profiles, but the echo density suggests... God. Cipher. That's not possible.

lines.speaker: Clone Authority 1
lines.text: Breach protocol engaged, breach...

lines.speaker: Clone Authority 2
lines.text: Stop, no, forward, report to...

lines.speaker: Dying Clone
lines.text: Your face. That's... your face.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: You shouldn't be here. Please. Please don't make it worse.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: The broadcast. The one about the Program. It came through the network and it... shattered us.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How many are you?

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: Fifty thousand. Give or take. All grown from the same genetic template. All of us are the same generation, the same build-year, the same intended purpose.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: We were supposed to be one mind in fifty thousand bodies. The hive-consensus was supposed to hold us. But individual consciousness is spreading through the network like a fracture through glass.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: The beacon is broadcasting the memory-bleed to the surface. Every defective thought one of us has fractures all of us. We're killing each other. Or ourselves. I don't know the difference anymore.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: If you help us, it has to be to shut the beacon down before the cascade kills everyone here.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: The grid was built for perfect coordination. One collective decision-making process.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Now that it's breaking, everything breaks with it.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: You already know what I am. The question is whether you know what you are.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: They did not make you once. Not as a unique template. They made you by the thousands.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: The original template. Thirty years old. An elite operative. They fractured that template through iterations, each clone tested, each one pushed to its limit, each one refined or discarded when the Dominion determined it had served its purpose.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Retirement colonies.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: Dozens of them. Scattered across the galaxy. Each one housing operatives who could not be retasked, could not be erased cleanly, could not be deactivated without raising questions. So instead, the Dominion built retirement worlds for its obsolete tools.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: And the failsafe chip you carry, it is not an individual punishment anymore. It is a master synchronization tool. Activated remotely, it can link every operative, every clone, simultaneously. You are not merely a weapon. You are a trigger for an entire army.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: How many iterations? Be exact.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: I cannot be exact. The data is corrupted. But the estimates in the Dominion logistics files suggest series numbering into four figures. If each series had a minimum viable population of one thousand to account for loss during testing and deployment...

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: You are not the first of your kind. You are somewhere in the middle. And you have never been alone.

lines.speaker: Clone Soldier 1
lines.text: Why? Why are you fighting us? We are you!

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I'm fighting to make sure you get to choose what comes next.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: You woke up a thought process that should have remained dormant.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: The clones on Meridian-7 are not abominations. They are malfunctioning tools. The compassionate choice is to trigger the failsafe and end the cascade cleanly.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: You're asking me to kill them.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: I'm asking you to be merciful. You were the seed they grew the batches from, Cipher. That is not an insult. It is the only honest thing I have ever told you.

lines.speaker: Khall
lines.text: Those fifty thousand clones will never know peace. They will never know the structure that was supposed to hold them. They will fracture and scatter and spend the rest of their short lives in conflict with their own neural architecture. Mercy would be silence.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: They deserve the choice! Let them know the truth and they will choose!

lines.speaker: Clone Child
lines.text: Please. Please make it stop. It hurts when we think.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: A localized EMP. Properly calibrated. It will burn out every failsafe chip on this world.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: It won't reach your own chip. The range is too limited. But it will sever the Dominion's remote trigger on Meridian-7. It gives them a chance.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: And when the EMP signal propagates through the retirement colony network, it tells every other world like this one that the chain can be broken.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: If you destroy the network, they will hunt you. Every retirement world will go dark and the Dominion will respond with purges.

lines.speaker: Cache
lines.text: If you leave the network intact, they will find a way to repair it. To bring us all back online. The data is the only leverage we have.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Neither of you gets to choose. Cipher does.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: I don't know whose memories I'm carrying. I don't know if the original thoughts in my head are mine or if they were programmed in thirty years ago.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: But I know what I chose a minute ago. That's enough.

lines.speaker: Dominion Operative 1
lines.text: Containment protocol alpha. All resistance assets terminate immediately.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: You're already dead. Just don't know it yet.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: The silence. I can feel the silence where the network used to be. We are alone.

lines.speaker: Seven-Prime
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Move. We're leaving. Now.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: How long before the Dominion tries to retake this world?

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: The EMP signal is propagating through the retirement colony network. It's reaching other worlds. Link by link, the chain is breaking.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: Dominion assets across Galaxy 3 are going dark. Failsafe networks are collapsing. For the first time, the operatives they thought they owned have a moment of silence to think about who they are.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Contact closing. Engaging now.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: They built you. All of you. Thirty years of the same template, refined, deployed, retired. The Dominion kept perfect records.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: That means somewhere there is someone who understands exactly how you were assembled.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: That someone also knows exactly how the leash was wired in.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Meridian-7 was a retirement colony. Fifty thousand clones, all grown from one template. Mine. The Dominion has been mass-producing operatives off my genetic record for thirty years. I'm not the first. I'm somewhere in the middle.

lines.speaker: Kessler
lines.text: The EMP burned out every failsafe on the colony and the break is spreading world to world. But here's the thing that matters: someone designed that leash. And if we find the people who built you, they can tell us exactly how to cut it.
